::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-9}
I have studied and/or lived in Nigeria, Australia, and the UK. My first degree was a BPharm at University of Uyo in 2014. Thereafter, I did an MPH degree at University of Melbourne in 2021 through an Australia Awards scholarship. My thesis was a [cost-effectiveness analysis](http://edifofon.com/blog/2022/brisc-cost-effectiveness-published/) of iron interventions for anaemia among Bangladeshi children. 

My work to date has been in public health, economic evaluation, and health decision science. Some of these include work on [scabies in Fiji](http://edifofon.com/papers/journal-articles/bigshift-scabiesSSTI-costs/); [COVID policy](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama-health-forum/article-abstract/2782622) in Australia, COVID public health measures in Malaysia, [COVID vaccine boosters](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2023.11.14.23298536v1) in Pacific countries, molecular testing for malaria and arboviruses in Papua New Guinea, and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines in developing countries.

Currently, I doing [Wellcome PhD](https://pheds-dtc.ac.uk/cohort-eight/) in Decision Science at The University of Sheffield. Most of my time in the next few years will be spent on analysis of cancer data or modelling cancer screening interventions. If you navigate to [Research](http://edifofon.com/research/) section of this website, you will see data and code from projects where I did a substantial part of the primary analysis.
:::
